clue.text: Stratemeyer's take on Thomas and Frank?

definitions.text: Stratemeyer's take on Thomas and Frank?

parts.words: Stratemeyer's take on Thomas and Frank?
parts.note: Edward Stratemeyer's syndicate created the boy detectives Frank and Joe; the clue pretends Thomas the Wessex novelist was Frank's brother, both sharing one surname

explanation.surface: A question about how a publisher reimagined two men called Thomas and Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas suggests the novelist of Wessex; Frank is one of the teenage sleuths in the Stratemeyer Syndicate's series, which shares his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stratemeyer Syndicate produced the juvenile detective series about the brothers Frank and Joe, whose surname is also the novelist Thomas's.

clue.text: Play with new competition from historian

parts.note: to play with something is to toy with it
a bee is a gathering for a contest, as in a spelling bee

explanation.surface: Someone toys with a fresh contest put on by a historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Toynbee was the British historian who wrote A Study of History.

clue.text: A bit of untended garden in Lear

indicators.note: only a small piece of the following words is wanted, so the solver looks inside them for a run of letters

explanation.surface: A neglected patch of garden appears in a production of King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar, Gloucester's legitimate son, is a leading character in Shakespeare's King Lear.

clue.text: Lawrence's funeral torch

definitions.meaning: a novel by D. H. Lawrence, published in 1922
the tall mullein plant, whose dried stalks dipped in tallow were once carried as torches at funerals

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the title of D. H. Lawrence's 1922 novel and a folk name for great mullein, a plant once burnt as a funeral taper.

clue.text: Never judge a book by this cover

definitions.text: Never judge a book by this cover

parts.words: Never judge a book by this cover
parts.note: the proverb about appearances is taken literally: the loose paper wrapper around a hardback is what the reader must not judge by

explanation.surface: The familiar proverb warning against judging by appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper jacket wrapped around a hardback book is called this kind of cover or jacket.

clue.text: Cymbeline character suggests America is supporting new Lib era

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath, so the America part comes at the bottom
new tells us the words Lib era are to be made new by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character hints that America is propping up a fresh Liberal era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LIBERA to BELARI; 'is supporting' puts US beneath it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Belarius is the banished lord in Shakespeare's Cymbeline who brings up the king's stolen sons.

clue.text: Some lawyer made a play by Lorca

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A solicitor has written a drama by the Spanish playwright Lorca.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerma is Federico García Lorca's 1934 tragedy about a childless woman in rural Spain.

clue.text: Zanuck screenplay for tale of old sea captain on island

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: Noah, who steered his vessel through the Flood, is the oldest of sea captains
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A film writer's script tells the story of an ancient mariner on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is a small Channel Island near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Darryl F. Zanuck wrote the story for the 1928 Warner Bros. Flood epic of that title.

clue.text: Ms Murdoch topped by big Egyptian deity

indicators.note: in a down answer the topping piece goes above the other

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a label for large clothes
Iris Murdoch was the Anglo-Irish novelist

explanation.surface: The novelist Iris Murdoch is overshadowed by a huge Egyptian god.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the ancient Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: Ancestral Christmas tree, a present from Norway

definitions.text: Ancestral Christmas tree, a present from Norway

parts.words: Ancestral Christmas tree, a present from Norway
parts.note: points not to the fir Norway sends London each year but to the great ash of Norse myth, an ancestor of all trees

explanation.surface: The Christmas tree Norway gives each year, described as a family heirloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Norway gives London a Christmas tree for Trafalgar Square every year; the clue's tree is the older mythical one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the immense ash Yggdrasil links the nine worlds, making it the Scandinavian ancestor of the world tree.

clue.text: Koestler noted those of chance ()

parts.note: Arthur Koestler's 1972 book on the origins of coincidence; chance stands for coincidence in his title

explanation.surface: Arthur Koestler wrote about the origins of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Koestler's book The Roots of Coincidence studied the sources of chance events.

clue.text: Novelist gets mixed drink at bar

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of the drink are shaken up into a new order

parts.note: gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A writer orders a cocktail at the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'at' are links; 'mixed' looks like part of the cocktail picture but is the anagram signal for the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Baring was an English novelist and man of letters of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Stegner gave his vassal equal billing

definitions.text: Stegner gave his vassal equal billing

parts.words: Stegner gave his vassal equal billing
parts.note: Wallace Stegner's novel about Joe Hill pairs two figures in its title, the second being a slave or vassal

explanation.surface: A writer gave his servant equal credit on the poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallace Stegner's novel The Preacher and the Slave names the minister alongside the slave, giving both equal place in the title.

clue.text: More, they say, produced it in extended wardrobe

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone made something and put it inside a long wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas More wrote a history of the reign of the fifth king of that name, so 'More' is the author, not the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's History of King Richard III opens with the death of the boy king's father, Edward IV, and his own work is credited with that history.

clue.text: Part for method actor. Or methodist

definitions.meaning: a role a Methodist would play, the follower of John Wesley
a member of the church founded by John Wesley

explanation.definitionFit: Followers of John Wesley were called after him; the term names a member of that denomination and a role for one.

clue.text: He wrote over there in France

definitions.text: He wrote over there in France

parts.words: He wrote over there in France
parts.note: over there in French is La-bas, the title of a novel by a French decadent writer

explanation.surface: A man did some writing while away in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Joris-Karl Huysmans wrote the novel La-bas, meaning over there, about satanism in Paris.

clue.text: Shavian heroine apparently in domestic service in France

definitions.text: Shavian heroine apparently in domestic service in France

parts.words: Shavian heroine apparently in domestic service in France
parts.note: Shaw's heroine was the Maid of Orleans; maid read as a housemaid puts her in domestic service in France

explanation.surface: One of Shaw's heroines seems to have been working as a servant in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play about Joan of Arc, called the Maid of Orleans, gives its heroine the title role.

clue.text: Poet said to be very fond of decorative trimmings

parts.note: to be very fond of something is to love it
lace is an ornamental fabric used for trimmings

explanation.surface: A poet is reported to adore frilly edging.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was the seventeenth-century Cavalier poet of To Althea, from Prison.

clue.text: "In this green room was a closet, with a —— and a curtain before it" (Samuel Richardson, Pamela)

definitions.text: "In this green room was a closet, with a —— and a curtain before it" (Samuel Richardson, Pamela)

parts.words: "In this green room was a closet, with a —— and a curtain before it" (Samuel Richardson, Pamela)
parts.note: a quotation from Richardson's novel with a gap where a kind of glazed, framed door fits

explanation.surface: A line from Pamela describing a closet in a green room.
explanation.definitionFit: Richardson's sentence names a door with a glazed frame like a window, the word missing from the quotation.

clue.text: Part as climbing provincial governor

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means the letters of Part as are read upwards, from the bottom

explanation.surface: An actor takes a role as an ambitious regional ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns PARTAS upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Persia the governor of a province was called a satrap.

clue.text: Mitchell character greatly admired by O'Hara

definitions.text: Mitchell character greatly admired by O'Hara

parts.words: Mitchell character greatly admired by O'Hara
parts.note: in Margaret Mitchell's Gone with the Wind, Scarlett O'Hara pines for Ashley, whose surname is wanted

explanation.surface: A character from Margaret Mitchell's novel whom O'Hara adores.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashley Wilkes is the gentleman in Gone with the Wind whom Scarlett O'Hara loves for most of the book.

clue.text: Poet may get on as novelist

definitions.text: Poet may get on as novelist

parts.words: Poet may get on as novelist
parts.note: the poet's surname, with on added at its end, becomes the surname of the Treasure Island novelist

explanation.surface: A poet might succeed by writing novels instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallace Stevens is the American poet; adding ON gives Robert Louis Stevenson.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallace Stevens was the American modernist poet, and adding two letters to his surname gives that of the Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson.

clue.text: Endless version of poet got the bird

definitions.text: Endless version of poet got the bird

parts.words: Endless version of poet got the bird
parts.note: Poe's poem, whose black visitor repeats Nevermore without end, gave the poet a famous bird

explanation.surface: An overlong version of a poet's work was booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got the bird' looks like being jeered, but it points to Poe's poem with its title bird and refrain Nevermore.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe's best-known poem is about a black bird that answers every question with Nevermore.

clue.text: Beer with a degree of acidity, seen first in Phoenicia

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
pH is the scale measuring how acid a solution is

explanation.surface: A slightly sour beer first brewed in ancient Phoenicia.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-shaped sign that heads the Phoenician alphabet, ancestor of Hebrew and Greek letters, is called aleph.

clue.text: Galsworthy's abounding on the street — that means trouble

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece placed on another comes after it, so abounding follows the street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
rife means abounding or widespread

explanation.surface: Something common on the street means there will be bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galsworthy's' also hints at the answer: John Galsworthy wrote a play about an industrial dispute with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict and discord, the sense of trouble between people.

clue.text: Weighty epic. Troy weighty

parts.note: troy weight is a system for gold, so a Troy-weighty epic is Homer's long poem about the siege of Troy

explanation.surface: A heavy epic poem measured in troy weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's great epic about the Trojan War is named after Ilion, another name for Troy.

clue.text: Shipbuilder's eldest. Sailed in

parts.note: the shipbuilder is Noah, and his eldest son was among those who sailed in the vessel during the Flood

explanation.surface: The eldest child of a boatbuilder who sailed aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Shem is counted as Noah's eldest son, who went into the ark with his father.

clue.text: A vigil recorded by Rodgers? ()

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over a body before burial

explanation.surface: A night watch captured on a record by Rodgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying up without sleep is the state of a watcher, and a song by Rodgers carries that word in its title.

clue.text: Daughter of Zeus badly atrophied

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of atrophied are put together in a wrong, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A child of the king of the gods has wasted away.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the goddess of love is the daughter of Zeus and Dione.

clue.text: The union guys with side collapsing they are tragic characters

parts.note: taken as written
EU is the abbreviation for European Union
men are guys

indicators.note: collapsing means the word side falls apart and its letters re-form in another order

explanation.surface: The trade union men, with their faction falling apart, are tragic figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges SIDE to IDES at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies of Greek myth appear as the chorus in Aeschylus's tragedy named after their gentler title, the kindly ones.
